mechanism_narrative: The sharp decline in WORKPLACES over the last two weeks will reduce weekday trip chaining into retail and recreation, so RETAIL_REC will fall further over the next four weeks as commuting-linked discretionary visits remain weak.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not below its last-28-day mean despite WORKPLACES staying below 0 or declining further.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility stays elevated while TRANSIT remains depressed, households are substituting home-based time for out-of-home shopping and entertainment, which suppresses RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -5 and RESIDENTIAL stays above +5
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after TRANSIT drops below -5 while RESIDENTIAL remains above +5.

mechanism_narrative: A one-week deterioration in PARKS mobility below its recent trend signals weaker outdoor leisure demand, and that softening spills into discretionary retail visits with a one-week lag.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by at least 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not weaken in the week after PARKS drops by at least 5 points from one week to the next.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both move down together, the city is in a soft-restriction or high-friction commuting regime that reduces in-person shopping access and keeps RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both negative for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days after two straight weeks with both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES below zero.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently high GROCERY_PHARM indicates spending is being absorbed by essential errands instead of discretionary retail, so RETAIL_REC will stay below its prior four-week average over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM remains above +40.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS combined with higher RESIDENTIAL mobility implies a weather- or leisure-driven stay-local pattern that converts outdoor time into nearby purchases, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS is positive for two weeks and RESIDENTIAL exceeds +8
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days after PARKS stays positive and RESIDENTIAL is above +8.

mechanism_narrative: Once TRANSIT recovers from negative territory, access to shopping districts improves with a short lag and RETAIL_REC turns higher over the next week, but only if WORKPLACES is not simultaneously collapsing.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses from below 0 to above 0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week after TRANSIT crosses above 0, or it falls when WORKPLACES is stable or rising.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of weaker TRANSIT and weaker WORKPLACES is a leading indicator of reduced discretionary trips, so retail activity will underperform its recent baseline across the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not below its last-four-week mean over the next 28 days while both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below their last-four-week means.
